strategy.summary: Reproduce the pandas GH#66549 bug by building the buggy revision d77e7af6890b from source and running the four new tests containing 'nat_sentinel'. On the buggy revision, int64 arithmetic that lands exactly on iNaT returns NaT instead of raising, so the tests fail. On the fixed revision (the PR head, hash not given in the evidence) add_overflowsafe raises OverflowError and the tests pass. The bug is pure integer logic in a Cython kernel, so it should not depend on architecture, BLAS or threading. Dependency versions are not documented, so the environment uses current releases that are compatible with this era's tree, and that choice is stated rather than inferred.

build_commands: pip install cython meson-python meson 'versioneer[toml]' numpy python-dateutil tzdata pytest hypothesis
git checkout d77e7af6890b && git submodule update --init --recursive (if present)
pinned_because: NumPy: no documented constraint and no era table entry, so the current NumPy release is chosen; this is a choice, not an inferred era constraint.
python-dateutil, tzdata, Cython: unbounded in the evidence; current releases chosen and stated as choices, not era-inferred pins.
Build uses --no-build-isolation, so the build-time packages (cython, meson-python, meson, numpy, versioneer) must already be installed in the active environment before the editable build.

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/arithmetic/test_datetime64.py::TestDatetime64Arithmetic::test_dt64arr_add_td_lands_on_nat_sentinel (units s, ms, us, ns; box_with_array); pandas/tests/arithmetic/test_timedelta64.py::TestTimedeltaArraylikeAddSubOps::test_tdi_sub_lands_on_nat_sentinel (units s, ms, us, ns); pandas/tests/arrays/test_period.py::test_period_add_int_lands_on_nat_sentinel; pandas/tests/scalar/timestamp/test_arithmetic.py::TestTimestampArithmetic::test_addsub_td_lands_on_nat_sentinel_raises (units s, ms, us, ns)
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision d77e7af6890b: each -k nat_sentinel case fails because the operation returns NaT (no exception), so pytest.raises reports 'DID NOT RAISE'. Fixed revision: the same cases pass, because add_overflowsafe raises OverflowError ('Overflow in int64 addition') for array paths and the scalar path raises OutOfBoundsDatetime. The transition from fail to pass is the success criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import pandas as pd; print(pd.Timestamp.min + pd.Timedelta(-1, 'ns'))"  (buggy: NaT; fixed: an exception)

input_output_examples.expected_output: raises OverflowError with message 'Overflow in int64 addition'
raises OverflowError with message 'Overflow in int64 addition'

risks: The fix and the tests are specific to the int64 kernel, so the bug is expected on any platform. Nothing in the evidence shows it needs a particular architecture, sanitiser, BLAS or thread count, but this is not verified on other platforms.

The scalar test expects OutOfBoundsDatetime with the message 'Out of bounds .* timestamp: -9223372036854775808', while the array tests expect OverflowError with 'Overflow in int64 addition'. Whether Timestamp.__add__ converts the OverflowError into OutOfBoundsDatetime is not stated in the evidence, so the scalar test's exact exception on the fixed revision is uncertain.
The commit message and test comments say the pre-fix behaviour was 'used to come back as NaT'. The exact pre-fix error text beyond 'Overflow in int64 addition' is not given.
Units other than s, ms, us, ns and non-UTC timezone variants are not covered by the evidence. The reproducer only exercises the listed units and UTC.
The fixed-revision hash is not given in the evidence. It is the PR head (GH#66602) and must be checked out separately to confirm the transition.
The PR date is blank, so the matching era of NumPy and other dependencies cannot be checked from the evidence. Current releases are used as a choice.

The buggy build must be compiled from source. An import failure or a stale editable build would fail the tests for reasons unrelated to the bug, so the build must be confirmed before reading the test results.
The new tests import iNaT from pandas._libs.tslibs. If that import is not available at the buggy revision, the test modules will fail at collection, not at the assertion.

oracle.reference_source: PR GH#66602 test diff (the four added test functions), commit message referencing GH#66549
oracle.why: The check is an exception type and message match, not a numerical tolerance. The int64 result either equals iNaT and must raise, or it does not.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On d77e7af6890b the array and scalar operations at iNaT+1 shifted by -1 unit return NaT without raising. pytest.raises(OverflowError) or pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsDatetime) then reports 'DID NOT RAISE', so the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision add_overflowsafe raises OverflowError('Overflow in int64 addition') when the int64 result equals NPY_DATETIME_NAT, so the array tests pass. The scalar test passes if Timestamp converts this to OutOfBoundsDatetime with the expected message.
